title: What Is a CIN Number? Full Form, Format and How to Check It
summary: What is a CIN number? Learn the CIN full form, 21-character format, how to check a company CIN online and how it is allotted after incorporation.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


###


Key Takeaways


- **CIN full form:** Corporate Identification Number
- **Issued by:** Registrar of Companies under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
- **Length:** 21 alphanumeric characters
- **Who receives it:** Companies incorporated in India
- **Used for:** Company identification, MCA records and statutory disclosures


After incorporation with the[Registrar of Companies](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-roc-registrar-of-companies/) , every Indian company receives a Corporate Identification Number. Like an identification number for an individual, a CIN helps distinguish one incorporated company from another in official records.


Knowing your CIN number is important for legal compliance and company verification. It appears on filings submitted to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) and on specified company communications. This guide explains the CIN full form, format, purpose, compliance requirements and online verification process.


##


**What Is a CIN Number?**


CIN stands for Corporate Identification Number. It is a unique 21-character alphanumeric identifier allotted by the ROC when a company is incorporated under the Companies Act.


Companies that receive a CIN include:


- [One Person Companies](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/one-person-company-opc/)
- Private and public limited companies
- Companies owned by the Government of India or a state government
- Nidhi companies
- [Section 8 companies](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/section-8-company/)


An[LLP](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/limited-liability-partnership-llp-company/) does not receive a CIN. It receives a Limited Liability Partnership Identification Number, or LLPIN, instead.


A CIN confirms that the company has been incorporated and identifies its recorded characteristics. It does not replace licences, tax registrations or sector-specific approvals that may be required before the company starts a regulated activity.


***Also Read:[Private Limited Company: Meaning and Registration](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/private-limited-company-explained/)***


##


**CIN Number Format: How to Read Its 21 Characters**


A CIN is not a random string. Its letters and numbers indicate the company’s listing status, industry code, state, incorporation year, company type and registration number.


For example:` U12345DL2020PLC098765`


CIN Section Meaning


U Listing status


12345 Industry code


DL State code


2020 Year of incorporation


PLC Company type


098765 Registration number


> The first character is generally **U** for an unlisted company or **L** for a listed company. The last six digits form the company’s ROC registration number.


##


Why Is the CIN Number Important?


CIN is more than a simple registration code, as it represents the official legal identity of an organisation registered under the Companies Act in India. The number serves multiple purposes, including;


1. **Establishes a Unique Company Identity:** The CIN uniquely identifies an organisation while recording its recognition by the[Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)](https://www.mca.gov.in/content/mca/global/en/home.html) . CIN confirms that the company is legally incorporated, registered in a specific state, and falls under a defined category. Without this number, the organisation cannot legally operate in the country.


2. **Supports Mandatory Disclosures:** Under Section 12 of the Companies Act, 2013, companies must print prescribed details, including the CIN, on business letters, billheads, letter papers, notices and other official publications.


3. **Improves Company Verification:** Stakeholders can use a CIN to locate the company’s master data on the MCA portal. Available records may include incorporation status, registered office, directors and capital details. It should not be treated as a standalone assessment of the company’s financial health or creditworthiness.


4. **Supports Tax, Banking and KYC Processes:** CIN is distinct from PAN and GSTIN, but banks, tax authorities and payment providers may use it with other incorporation documents to verify a company. A[business PAN](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/business-pan-card-how-to-apply-online-documents-required/) identifies the entity for income-tax purposes, while a GSTIN applies when GST registration is required.


5. **Helps with Business Banking:** Banks may request the CIN and Certificate of Incorporation while reviewing a company account or credit application. The final documentation depends on the bank, product and risk assessment. See the usual[corporate account requirements](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/corporate-account/) for a broader checklist.


##


**Common Company-Type Abbreviations in a CIN**


Under Section 5 of the CIN, a series of terms are used and knowing them is important if you want a complete understanding of what CIN number means. These are;


- **FLC** : Financial Lease Company as Public Limited Company
- **FTC** : Subsidiary of a Foreign Company as Private Limited Company
- **GAP** : General Association Public
- **GAT** : General Association Private
- **GOI** : Companies owned by the Government of India
- **NPL** : Not-for-Profit License Company (Section 8 Company)
- **OPC** : One Person Company
- **PLC** : Public Limited Company
- **PTC** : Private Limited Company
- **SGC** : Companies owned by the State Government
- **ULL** : Public Limited Company with Unlimited Liability
- **ULT** : Private Company with Unlimited Liability


##


**CIN Disclosure Requirements and Penalties**


The company receives its CIN automatically when incorporation is approved, so there is no separate CIN application to ignore or miss. The compliance risk arises when a company fails to display its required particulars or update relevant company records.


Under Section 12(8) of the Companies Act, a default involving the disclosure requirements in Section 12 can attract a penalty of ₹1,000 for every day the default continues, subject to a maximum of ₹1 lakh for the company and every officer in default.


Apart from penalties, incorrect or missing company details can create problems during due diligence, banking, regulatory filings and vendor onboarding. CIN does not determine GST rates or replace the company’s separate tax obligations.


##


**How to Get a CIN Number Through Company Incorporation**


You do not apply for a CIN separately. The ROC allots it when the company’s incorporation application is approved and the Certificate of Incorporation is issued.


The general process is:


1. **Choose the company name and structure:** Select the proposed name and appropriate company type.
2. **Obtain digital signatures:** Proposed subscribers and directors obtain the required Digital Signature Certificates. Director Identification Numbers may be requested through the incorporation process where applicable.
3. **Prepare incorporation documents:** Draft the[Memorandum of Association](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/memorandum-of-association-moa/) and Articles of Association, along with identity, address and registered-office documents.
4. **File SPICe+ and linked forms:** Submit the incorporation application through the MCA portal.
5. **Receive the Certificate of Incorporation:** After approval, the ROC issues the certificate containing the company’s CIN. Submitting the forms alone does not create the CIN; ROC approval is required.

##


How to Do a CIN Number Check Online


If you want to verify a company CIN number, you can easily do a CIN number check on the MCA website.


Follow these steps.


**Step 1:** Visit the Ministry of Corporate Affairs website (www.mca.gov.in).


**Step 2:** Go to MCA Services.


**Step 3:** Select View Company/LLP Master Data.


**Step 4:** Enter the company name.


**Step 5:** Complete the CAPTCHA and click Search.


The system will display the CIN number of the company along with its registration details.

##


**Conclusion**


The Corporate Identification Number is an important identifier for companies incorporated in India. Understanding the CIN full form, structure and online-check process helps businesses maintain accurate records and allows customers, lenders and other stakeholders to verify company details.


After incorporation, companies may separately need[GST registration](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-registration-online-process-documents/) ,[Udyam registration](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/udyam-registration-online/) or sector-specific licences, depending on their activities. These registrations serve different purposes and do not replace the CIN.

FAQs


####


**What is CIN number?**


A CIN number is a 21-digit alphanumeric code assigned to companies registered in India by the Registrar of Companies under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.


####


**Is CIN the same as company registration number?**


Not exactly. The last six digits are the ROC registration number, while the complete CIN contains additional information about the company.


####


**Can I change my company’s CIN Number?**


Yes. The CIN may change when an encoded characteristic changes, such as listing status, company type or the state of the registered office. A routine change in directors does not by itself change the CIN.


####


**How can I find a company’s CIN?**


To find the CIN, visit the MCA website and look for MCA Services and navigate to View Company/LLP Master Data. In the search bar, enter the existing company name, fill in the Captcha code, and hit search to get the CIN number.


####


**Which companies are eligible to obtain a CIN number?**


Public and private limited companies incorporated in India are eligible to get a Corporate Identification Number (CIN). Other types of organisations, like partnership firms and sole proprietorship firms, do not need to have a CIN. But LLPs are not eligible to receive a CIN number.


####


**Can two companies have the same CIN?**


It is unique to each company and is issued only once at the time of the company’s incorporation, and is permanently assigned to that organisation. Even if the company changes its registered name, address, or directors, the CIN remains the same.
